audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows contradicted the prose printed beside them. whys[0] says level 1 is 'immediately proxy his wave before he can establish lane presence' but the chart gave it to Jax; whys[2] says 'Jax wins any trade where you plant your feet at level 3' and whys[3] says he 'dominates direct duels through levels 4 and 5' but the chart gave both to Singed; whys[4] says 'neither of you can cleanly kill the other' and whys[5] says 'both sides are spiking simultaneously' but the chart called those Jax and Singed rather than Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart (Singed, Skill, Jax, Jax, Skill, Skill, Singed) reproduces the prose row for row and sits properly against a 55.62% Emerald+ win rate over 1717 games.
audit.corrected: Whole chart realigned to the packet as one atomic group in both layers, with the affected phase whys rewritten to match their new sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty 7.5/10 and 'Tricky' on a 55.62% favoured matchup, and the level-6 row was generic 'ult-ghost-proxy' text that never said what Jax's ultimate actually does.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110/100/90; its armour and magic resist come from ACTIVATING it, which makes level 6 a timed window you can wait out rather than a permanent stat gap.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10, diff FAV, difficulty and final-rating rows matched; level 6 now names Grandmaster-at-Arms, its 110s cooldown and the fact the resists are an active window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Counter Strike is described as negating 'your Fling auto-damage' and 'your auto-attacks'. Riot's text is 'dodge all incoming attacks' — basic attacks. Poison Trail is not an attack and is not dodged, so against Singed specifically Counter Strike's dodge does almost nothing and only the stun matters; the page never says this. (b) Grandmaster-at-Arms's armour and magic resist are attributed to its PASSIVE in four places ('his R passive armor', 'his R armor bonus'). Riot: the passive is 'Every third consecutive attack deals additional Magic Damage'; the resists come from activating the ability. That turns a permanent stat wall into a 110-second timed window you can simply outlast. (c) Mega Adhesive grounds and Leap Strike is a dash flagged in Jax's own kit as 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny' — the glue shuts his gap-closer off entirely, and this was never stated.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon descriptions for Jax E/R/Q and Singed W.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike re-described as dodging attacks but not Poison Trail; the ultimate's resists re-attributed to its activation with the 110s cooldown; Mega Adhesive grounding Leap Strike (8s) written in as the decisive interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Jax cooldown appeared anywhere; 'Counter Strike has a short enough cooldown to be present in almost every trade' was the closest the page got.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9, Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 at 700 range, Empower 7/6/5/4/3, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90.
audit.corrected: Rank-appropriate numbers written into the phase whys, the cooldown block, the tracked-ability do and the spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower is an auto-attack reset and nothing on the page mentioned it — the reader is told to watch for the Counter Strike cast, when the real tell is the Empower wind-up that opens his burst.
audit.why: Riot flags Empower with autoReset; the _missing file carries the same rule for this pairing.
audit.corrected: The Empower wind-up written in as the step-back cue in the Critical Don'ts and in what Jax wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Grandmaster's At-Arms' appears twice; Riot's name is 'Grandmaster-at-Arms'.
audit.corrected: Renamed in wants.foe[2] and in the late-game paragraph.

edits.before: You lose most level-1 duels — set up the proxy game instead. Identify how Jax contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: He has no stun yet and Leap Strike (8s) alone cannot trade — proxy his wave and poison his minions before he owns any of the lane.

edits.before: Fling + glue starts punishing anyone who chases. Only take the trade when Jax's Counter Strike is down.
edits.after: Mega Adhesive grounds: in the glue, Leap Strike will not cast. Trade only when Counter Strike is spent.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jax must walk into your range.
edits.after: Counter Strike (13s at rank 3) stuns you where you stand, and that is the only trade he wants. Never plant your feet.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His scaling outpaces your early stats and Counter Strike (11s at rank 4) is up for nearly every trade. Proxy and ghost his jungle, do not duel.

edits.before: Ult-ghost-proxy is a macro weapon — you win by farming where he is not. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jax's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms (110s at rank 1) is an ACTIVE armour and MR window, not a passive — run poison through it until it expires, then re-engage.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Counter Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: Rylai's lands but so does his first item — both of you spike at once, and the first positional error decides it.

edits.before: Counter Strike dodges your auto-attacks and stuns you in place, which is every trade Jax wants — stay mobile and never commit while E is up.
edits.after: Counter Strike (13s at rank 3) dodges basic attacks, but Poison Trail is not one — the stun is the real threat, so never plant your feet near it.

edits.before: With Rylai's and Liandry's your poison rots him through his R passive armor; he needs three or four items to consistently win the 1v1 before your team collapses on him.
edits.after: With Rylai's and Liandry's your poison rots him through the armour Grandmaster-at-Arms grants on activation; he needs three or four items to win that duel cleanly.

edits.before: Fling his Q-leap when he bridges the gap — landing him behind you into your poison cloud resets the whole chase
edits.after: Glue his landing spot — grounded, Leap Strike (8s) will not fire — then Fling him back through your own poison cloud

edits.before: Land Counter Strike after the Q-leap so you are stunned and unable to Fling him away
edits.after: Open with an Empower auto-reset, then Counter Strike so the stun lands before your Fling

edits.before: Scale to two items where Grandmaster's At-Arms stacks let him burst through your tank stats before your poison finishes him
edits.after: Scale to two items where Grandmaster-at-Arms and Relentless Assault burst through your tank stats before the poison finishes him

edits.before: Counter Strike is live but baitable — Mega Adhesive roots him if he overextends chasing, making the trade even on burst.
edits.after: Counter Strike is baitable, and Mega Adhesive grounds — in the glue Leap Strike will not cast, so the chase ends where you choose.

edits.before: Insanity Potion's magic resistance partially blunts his R passive, but neither of you can cleanly kill the other without a big cooldown mistake.
edits.after: Insanity Potion's MR blunts Grandmaster-at-Arms, whose armour is an active on a 110s cooldown — neither of you kills the other without a big mistake.

edits.before: Rylai's plus Liandry's means your Poison Trail rots him through his R armor bonus faster than he can burst you before your team collapses on him.
edits.after: Rylai's plus Liandry's rot him through the armour Grandmaster-at-Arms grants on cast, faster than he can burst you before your team collapses on him.

edits.before: At level 1 Jax has no stun and his Q-leap alone is not enough to trade cleanly, so immediately go under his tower or behind his wave and start poisoning his minions — proxy this wave before he can establish any presence. At level 2 he gets Counter Strike, which is the entire danger of this lane: it negates your Fling auto-damage and stuns you in place, so the moment you see him start its animation, break off the chase and kite away. At level 3 your full kit is live but his Counter Strike stun wins any trade where you stand still — keep running and use Mega Adhesive to root him if he overextends chasing you, then re-engage only after the stun window expires.
edits.after: At level 1 Jax has no stun and his Q-leap alone is not enough to trade cleanly, so immediately go under his tower or behind his wave and start poisoning his minions — proxy this wave before he can establish any presence. Once he puts a point in Counter Strike (17s at rank 1), which is the entire danger of this lane: it dodges basic attacks but not Poison Trail — the stun is the threat, so the moment you see him start its animation, break off the chase and kite away. At level 3 your full kit is live but his Counter Strike stun wins any trade where you stand still — keep running and use Mega Adhesive to root him if he overextends chasing you, then re-engage only after the stun window expires.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Jax's best window against you: his damage scaling starts to outpace your early stats and Counter Strike has a short enough cooldown to be present in almost every trade. Do not fight him directly — proxy the wave, force him under his tower, and ghost through his jungle if he does not follow. At level 6 your Insanity Potion grants enough movement speed and magic resistance to make his Q-into-E combo less punishing, but his R passive armor and magic resistance mean the 1v1 is still a coin flip — win the lane through map pressure, not through dueling him at six.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Jax's best window against you: his damage scaling starts to outpace your early stats and Counter Strike is 11s at rank 4, up for almost every trade. Do not fight him directly — proxy the wave, force him under his tower, and ghost through his jungle if he does not follow. At level 6 your Insanity Potion grants enough movement speed and magic resistance to make his Q-into-E combo less punishing, but Grandmaster-at-Arms's activated armour and MR keep the 1v1 a coin flip — win the lane through map pressure, not through dueling him at six.

edits.before: With Rylai's Crystal Scepter your Poison Trail permanently slows him and makes every chase Jax starts suicidal — he runs into the cloud, you Fling him back through it, and Mega Adhesive roots him if he tries to leave. At two items his Grandmaster's At-Arms stacks are dangerous if he can land a clean stun, but Liandry's burns through his R armor bonus and the slow keeps him from getting the extended trade he needs. Play split-push and force him to answer you alone; if he brings help, your Ghost and Insanity Potion let you disengage through terrain and proxy the other side, bleeding his team's resources until they cannot protect both waves.

notes: Two mechanical facts on this page were backwards in a way that changes how the lane is played. First, Counter Strike dodges BASIC ATTACKS; Poison Trail is not an attack, so Jax's signature defensive tool does nothing to Singed's actual damage source — only the stun matters, and the page instead told the reader it 'negates your Fling auto-damage'. Second, Grandmaster-at-Arms's armour and MR are on the ACTIVE, not the passive (the passive is the every-third-attack magic damage), so level 6 is a window to outlast rather than a permanent stat wall. Also note Jax's Empower carries a derived 'dash' flag in the kit file — that is a tooltip-parsing misfire (Riot: 'charges his weapon with energy, causing his next attack to deal additional damage'), so Empower is treated only as the auto-reset it really is. Chart flipped in five rows to match the page's own whys and the packet. Cooldowns used: Jax Q 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 at 700, W 7/6/5/4/3, E 17/15/13/11/9, R 110/100/90.
